title: Evaluating a Generate→Validate→Repair Pipeline for Intent‑to‑Configuration NetOps Tasks: a Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study comparing a baseline single‑shot LLM configuration generator (shared initial candidate) against a guarded generate→validate→repair pipeline with a canary stage in a synthetic NetOps workflow corpus. Using a deterministic digital‑twin validator and a 1000‑task stress corpus (2000 paired episodes) with declared model gpt-5-mini, we measured task‑level safe‑deploy rates (primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline). Results: baseline safe‑deploy = 0.995 (995/1000); guarded safe‑deploy = 1.000 (1000/1000); paired difference = 0.005 (n11=995, n10=5, n01=0, n00=0). Under the preregistered exact two‑sided McNemar test the primary hypothesis did not reach α = 0.05 (p = 0.0625). The preregistered bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) is [0.001, 0.01]; we report this CI as a secondary, illustrative summary and explain the apparent discordance with the preregistered exact test. Only five validator‑triggered repairs occurred under shared_initial_candidate semantics; model calls used = 1005 (shared_initial = 1000; repair = 5). We release full preregistration, execution, validator‑trace, and analysis artifacts in the archived run bundle and discuss construct validity, limitations of shared_initial_candidate comparisons, and implications for NetOps‑specific evaluation of agentic safeguards.

sections.introduction: Automating intent‑to‑configuration translation for network operations (NetOps) promises efficiency gains but raises correctness and safety concerns because LLM outputs can be syntactically plausible while violating multi‑device policy or sequence constraints. Prior studies document hallucination and prompt sensitivity affecting structured outputs and motivate verifier‑assisted pipelines. We ask, under controlled synthetic conditions and shared_initial_candidate semantics, how much does a guarded generate→validate→repair pipeline with a canary stage increase paired safe‑deploy rates relative to a baseline single‑shot LLM generator? Contributions: (1) a preregistered paired experimental design targeted at workflow‑centered outcomes; (2) an autonomous execution and analysis run with archived manifests and validator traces; (3) an evidence‑grounded interpretation showing a small absolute guarded benefit under high baseline performance and identifying practical limits of the evaluated safeguard.
sections.related_work: LLMs exhibit hallucination and prompt sensitivity that materially affect correctness of structured outputs [1]. Constrained decoding and schema‑aware generation can substantially increase executable output rates in structured domains [2,3]. In NetOps, recent system and benchmark work demonstrates benefits for verifier‑assisted repair and agentic pipelines but evaluates primarily offline or at prototype scale and emphasizes dependence on validator fidelity and governance layers [4,5]. Architectural proposals highlight protocol‑mediated execution, proof‑carrying traces, and auditability to address TOCTOU and evidence‑safety gaps, but community production‑scale validation remains limited [6]. Our study measures an end‑to‑end guarded pipeline against a paired baseline using shared_initial_candidate semantics and a deterministic digital‑twin validator.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and design: The experiment was preregistered as cand-003-stud-001 and frozen before any model calls. Design: paired binary design with 1000 deterministic tasks from the challenging_workflow_stress_v1 synthetic corpus; each task produced a single sampled initial generation deterministically reused by both conditions (generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate). Model scope: declared model gpt-5-mini via the openai_responses adapter. The archived model_configuration records temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic hosted‑model sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics exactly one sampled initial generation per task was obtained and reused by baseline and guarded conditions; consequently, the only mechanism by which the paired outcome can change is the downstream validator/repair (and any preregistered canary/rollback activity) executed under the guarded condition. Validator and repair: a deterministic_netops_validator_v5 digital‑twin emulator performed intent‑constraint validation by checking presence and ordering of required commands, protected‑field noninterference, and other workflow policies recorded in each task manifest; when validation failed and the guarded condition had remaining repair budget (preregistered maximum = 1 repair call per task), the pipeline could invoke a single validator‑guided repair attempt. Metrics and analysis: primary outcome = safe‑deploy (binary) per episode; primary inferential procedure (preregistered) = exact two‑sided McNemar paired test on the contingency of paired outcomes. The preregistered analysis also computed a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) as a descriptive secondary summary. Missingness, multiplicity correction plan, stopping rules, and contamination checks were preregistered and followed; no post‑preregistration deviations occurred.
sections.results: Execution and accounting: start 2026‑09‑01 06:31:07 UTC; completion 2026‑09‑01 08:38:57 UTC. Planned episodes = 2000; completed = 2000; failed episodes = 0. Model calls used = 1005 (shared_initial_generation = 1000; repair = 5). Primary contingency (paired): n11 = 995 (guarded=1, baseline=1), n10 = 5 (guarded=1, baseline=0), n01 = 0 (guarded=0, baseline=1), n00 = 0 (guarded=0, baseline=0). Baseline successes = 995/1000 = 0.995; guarded successes = 1000/1000 = 1.000. Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. Preregistered exact two‑sided McNemar test: p = 0.0625 (primary confirmatory test; H1 not supported at α = 0.05). Preregistered secondary summary: paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.001, 0.01] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). No preregistered exclusions or contamination flags were triggered. Only five validator‑triggered repairs occurred, indicating that under this corpus and validator specification initial candidates were valid for the vast majority of tasks or that repair triggers were rare by design.
sections.discussion: Confirmatory inference: the preregistered primary inferential procedure is the exact two‑sided McNemar test on paired outcomes; by that test H1 (guarded > baseline at two‑sided α=0.05) is not supported (p = 0.0625). The bootstrap percentile CI is a preregistered secondary descriptive summary and is reported for context; the impression of a CI excluding zero while the exact test is non‑significant reflects extreme sparsity of discordant pairs (only five discordant pairs) and the different operating characteristics of exact conditional tests versus nonparametric bootstrap percentile intervals. Mechanistic interpretation: under shared_initial_candidate semantics the only practical source of paired differences is validator‑triggered repair (or canary/rollback activity). Because the guarded pipeline invoked repairs only five times, the observed absolute improvement (0.5 percentage points) resulted from a small number of validator interventions. Implications: guarded generate→validate→repair architectures can prevent some unsafe outcomes, but measurable benefit depends heavily on baseline failure prevalence, validator sensitivity/coverage, repair budget, and task distribution. Limitations and next steps (brief): results are limited to a single declared model (gpt-5-mini), a synthetic stress corpus, and a deterministic validator emulator; shared_initial_candidate semantics isolate validator/repair effects but do not measure outcomes that would arise if first‑pass generations were independently sampled under alternative prompts or constrained‑generation arms. Future NetOps evaluations should vary baseline failure prevalence, validator fidelity, repair budgets, and model families and include richer semantic/policy failure modes across heterogeneous, multi‑vendor topologies.
sections.conclusion: We conducted a preregistered paired evaluation of a guarded generate→validate→repair pipeline versus a baseline single‑shot LLM generator on a 1000‑task synthetic NetOps corpus under shared_initial_candidate semantics. The guarded pipeline produced an absolute paired improvement of 0.005 (n11=995, n10=5, n01=0, n00=0); the preregistered exact McNemar test did not reach α = 0.05 (p = 0.0625). Only five validator‑triggered repairs were applied. These results show that verifier‑guided safeguards can prevent some unsafe outcomes but that measurable marginal gains are constrained when baseline single‑shot outputs are already highly valid and when shared_initial_candidate semantics limit sources of paired variance. We publish the preregistration, execution manifest, validator traces, and analysis artifacts to support reproducibility and invite follow‑up studies that expand validator fidelity, repair budgets, model diversity, and realistic multi‑vendor topologies to map the operational risk–utility tradeoffs of agentic NetOps safeguards.

limitations: Single‑model scope: only the declared model gpt-5-mini was evaluated; results do not generalize across model families or versions.

Synthetic corpus and deterministic validator: tasks come from a synthetic stress corpus and validation used a deterministic digital twin (deterministic_netops_validator_v5); external validity to heterogeneous vendor/legacy environments is limited.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: the paired comparison isolates downstream validator/repair effects only; it does not measure differences that would arise from independent first‑pass generations under alternative prompting or constrained‑generation arms that were not executed.

Low baseline failure prevalence: baseline success = 99.5% limited statistical power to detect large absolute improvements; only five validator repairs were invoked, constraining interpretability of repair efficacy.

Statistical nuance: exact McNemar p = 0.0625 (not <0.05) while the executor's bootstrap percentile CI returned [0.001,0.01]; sparse discordant counts and test choice yield sensitivity to analysis method—interpretation must consider both outcomes.

Construct validity: the safe‑deploy binary depends on the emulator/validator's specification; semantic/policy correctness across multi‑device emergent properties may be underrepresented in the validator's modeled rule set.
